However, adding complexity by incorporating final-state interactions raises this value to approximately 1.6, in line with more recent measurements. Hadron production yields within these calculations exhibit a pattern that mirrors experimental observations as the quark's momentum fraction varies. Also, one observed feature in the ratio of hadrons with different compositions can be attributed to the presence of b bbar pairs in the hadronization medium.

Through number theory and combinatorial methods, we establish upper limits for specific expressions, which are key in defining the maximum number of elements in certain families of curves over finite fields.

Combining this approach with results from our previous work and those of other researchers, we are able to obtain improved upper bounds for specific mathematical sequences, including new records for sequences A002123, A002148, A002486, A002646, A002647, A002648, A002649, A002650, A002970, A003632, A003633, A003634, A003635, A003636, and A345967.

This paper outlines the evolution of High-Performance Computing (HPC) and concurrent cloud computing, highlighting how the latter has revolutionized computing by offering on-demand access to scalable computing resources. Although cloud providers have made significant investments in HPC clusters, a critical issue persists: geographical limitations hinder users from utilizing these resources due to substantial data transfer costs, associated with syncing local and cloud data. This problem is exacerbated by the vast sizes of typical HPC clusters. To address this challenge, this paper explores the potential of Storage-Area Network (SAN) enabled HPC cloud clusters, proposing a novel approach where users can access distributed data locally via SAN, thereby minimizing network latency and eliminating data synchronization expenses. A detailed analysis of the factors contributing to latency and bandwidth in SAN enabled HPC cloud clusters has been conducted, followed by a comparative study with traditional clustered network architectures, ultimately highlighting the performance benefits of SAN enabled HPC cloud clusters in minimizing latency.

This study delves into the effect of contextual knowledge on communication requirements in contextual linear bandit problems. By assessing various levels of contextual knowledge pre-existing at the encoder, our research gauges the additional information needed to reproduce the context distribution. This approach allows us to determine how existing knowledge impacts performance. Our theoretical findings include minimax optimal rates for contextual regret when contexts are fully transmitted, random, or compressed. Notably, we develop a novel contextual algorithm based on the extended linear model, outperforming previous methods and matching the theoretical optimality in settings with random contexts. Moreover, our algorithm's performance matches the minimax optimal rate in scenarios where contexts are fully transmitted, across both stochastic and adversarial environments.

The adoption of collaborative project frameworks like Agiles and Scrum by remote teams is increasingly prevalent, yet there's still a gap in comprehensive studies exploring their effectiveness under remote working conditions. To address this missing information, our research aims to explore the implications of collaborative project methodologies on the productivity and satisfaction of remote teams. Using web survey data collected from 418 teams collaborating on software development projects, our findings suggest that agile methodology usage is associated with enhanced project success, which in turn has a positive influence on both the satisfaction and self-reported work output of software developers working from home.

This project aims to develop streamlined value function assessments that reduce complexity for efficient learning in policy optimization. By leveraging optimal interpolation, we achieved results surpassing existing testable methods, particularly when training data is abundant. Moreover, our approach excels in policy optimization scenarios involving optimal interpolation.

Measurements of proton-lead (pPb) collisions at a center-of-mass energy of 5.02 TeV for data collected in 2013 show that the mean squared transverse momentum of hadrons with an electric charge, denoted as $p_{\text{T}}$, increases as elliptic flow ($v_2$) rises. This trend holds true for a wide range of $v_2$ values, from 0.02 to 0.15 and for a center-of-mass rapidity of 0.375 $\pm$ 0.075. Further analysis reveals that this relationship is consistent across different types of hadrons (specifically protons, kaons, and pions) and for rapidity values of 0 and 0.375. Additionally, a higher proton to pion ratio in $v_2$ is observed for hadrons with higher $p_{\text{T}}$. These findings are in agreement with predictions from hydrodynamic models that incorporate initial-state fluctuations.

This research investigates the properties of the Quaternion Linear Canonical Stockwell Transform, specifically addressing inequalities such as Uncertainty Principles, Leibniz, and product rules. A key contribution is the establishment of a sharp inequality for theQLCST transform, with applications in signal denoising and improvement. Notably, a new inequality is derived for Lipschitz continuous signals, building on these foundations.

Investigating the effectiveness of a simple binary power control approach in scaleable networks affected by broad-spectrum interference, we discovered that in terms of achieving high throughput, it performs closely to an optimal power control strategy, particularly under conditions of limited bandwidth and narrow interference patterns, whether they are random or deterministic. This finding allows us to model large scale networks with wide bandwidth and deterministic interference patterns using a performance metric based on a set of rules using only two power levels. This new analysis yields closed-form equations for key performance indicators such as coverage and capacity, significantly reducing the complexity of calculations from O(n) to constant, and substantially improving an existing approximation known as the large-system approximation. Additionally, we applied this new analysis to a common scenario of downlink cell grouping in cell partitioning to demonstrate its practical benefits.

A new simulation technique for particle-filled flows has been developed. This approach, called the FastSim, utilizes multi-step time advancement to shift and process small time-step tasks to fewer large time steps. As a result, FastSim achieves up to 50 times faster simulation times than the conventional method, with no compromise on results accuracy. We validated our approach by demonstrating its effectiveness with millions of particles in a test scenario.

This note is dedicated to the memory of Andrzej Schinzel, who passed away on March 14, 2023. We explore his significant contributions to number theory through our own research on the Diophantine equation 7^ n = a^ 3 + b^ 3 with positive integers a and b. This type of equation can be rewritten in the form y^ 3 = 7^ n x^ 2 + 7, where x, y, x^ 2 y are required to be non-zero. For n = 1, 2, we can find infinite solutions. On a positive note, the only solution with x^ 3 y not divisible by 49 (found by Schinzel in 1970) is with (x, y, n) = (2, 3, 2). Additionally, Schinzel in 1970 proved that if n is even and y is not divisible by 49, then y must be equal to 3. We could extend this result, showing that if n is even, there always exist infinitely many x such that the equation has a solution y with x^ 2 y not divisible by 49. Moreover, if n is a multiple of three, we can't find any solutions. Yet, if n isn't a multiple of three, infinite solutions exist. Some explicit examples are provided, and one result can be derived,

This paper delves into the complexities of tracking desired trajectories in real-time when hopping on an unstable and yielding surface. By utilizing a feedback control scheme, we demonstrate the effectiveness of maintaining stable motion and following a predefined path. Various hacking scenarios are examined to illustrate the benefits of this approach, including the impact of unexpected ground displacement and varying surface compliances. In a more practical setting, we apply this control method to a robotic hacker capable of following dynamic trajectories, even as it navigates an unstable and soft surface. By combining high-speed imaging with a robust control algorithm, we are able to examine the precision of this tracking in a realistic setting.

Using a novel 1/N^2 expansion approach with an analytical meson meson effective field theory, researchers have determined the charge radii of mesons at different orders of approximation. The study employs a spontaneous symmetry breaking pattern, a Gaussian functional integral approximation, and perturbation theory in the inverse square of a parameter, resulting in the extraction of a quark condensate value and the calculation of charge radii for various mesons to the one-loop order. Furthermore, the findings have implications for understanding the behavior of matter under extreme conditions, including the equation of state, particle diffusion, and the nature of the phase transition.

This research examines the significant deformation vibrations of a liquid droplet suspended in a surrounding gas, moving at a constant speed, and undergoing intense vibrational motion. We analyze this phenomenon using nonlinear theory, investigating how large deformations affect the movement, heat, and mass transfer of the liquid and surrounding gas. Our findings show that frequent vibrations result in improved transfer of heat and mass, but altered deformations can reduce this efficiency. A key discovery is that large deformations cause the liquid to gain an excess of surrounding gas, leading to an unexpected decrease in vibration frequency. This study extends the scope of previous research, which focused primarily on nearly spherical droplets with small deformations, and presents numerical results that illustrate the intricate relationships between deformation frequency, surface tension, and transfer rates.

Recent advancements in Natural Language Processing have outperformed many previous methods, yet the finest current models struggle with tasks involving negation in text. This paper investigates four aspects of negation: structure, compositionality, theory, and application, aiming to shed light on how negation affects language and enables its manipulation for tasks like NLP. Our analysis reveals concerning results, indicating that state-of-the-art models excel at mimicking human-like performance on basic tests but fall short on more complex tasks. This discrepancy suggests a discrepancy between the capabilities of these models and their performance on tasks that truly involve understanding negation.

Recent links between social networks and human language evolution suggest a structural similarity in their hierarchies. This paper introduces a new model, the Hierarchical Document Topic Model (HDTM), which adapts the Hidden Markov Model to extract hierarchical topic relationships from documents. HDTM generates a tree structure to represent topic connections, allowing for flexible analysis of various networks. A learning algorithm is developed to optimize the model's parameters, reconstructing both topic distributions and relationships. Utilizing the tree's topological properties, we apply HDTM to analyze Wikipedia category networks and demonstrate its effectiveness by comparing the model's structure to actual category relationships. Additionally, HDTM reveals unique topic relationships, such as overlapping functionality, not captured by traditional models.

To take full advantage of quantum annealing's potential, it's crucial to understand how to manage the annealing gap. By applying adiabatic quantum division of labor to distinguish between an isolating transition and a polynomial slow-down, we define and explore the concept of the gap structure, which could provide precise guidance for optimizing quantum annealing protocols. Unfortunately, directly observing the annealing gap's behavior is hindered by significant technical limitations in current quantum annealing hardware. Consequently, we shift our focus to studying the dynamics of a randomly generated instance solver, combined with minor quantum local search, on a moderately sized instance, and find evidence supporting the existence of an isolating transition within this hybrid approach.

When comparing and analyzing the differences between system traces, alignment techniques are commonly employed. Currently prevalent methods, such as Levenshtein-based alignments, differ from the realistic temporal sequences of actual process sequences. To address this discrepancy, this study introduces two novel alignments - infix and postfix alignments - that account for the temporal aspects of process sequences by inserting deletions at the beginning, end, or middle of process traces. Key properties of these new alignments are theoretically analyzed, and an iterative algorithm for finding optimal postfix alignments is proposed along with a data structure to ensure its efficiency. Through experiments, it's demonstrated that the algorithm can efficiently find the optimal postfix alignment in most cases, but may require more time in other scenarios. Furthermore, infix and postfix alignments can serve as alternatives to traditional alignments in process execution clustering, and our approach shows that clustering using these methods is more accurate than using the Levenshtein-based alignments.

To investigate calcium nickelates, we computed their electronic structure, incorporating strong correlations via the self-consistent SUHF method, considering both antiferromagnetic and non-magnetic order. Our computations reveal that incorporating spin polarization lowers the correlation strength sufficient to populate a narrow conduction band, potentially leading to superconductivity upon doping. Comparing our theoretical predictions to experimental data on the nickelates nickel oxide cluster's L-edge X-ray absorption and nickel K-edge XANES, we found good agreement.

We transform the periodic non-cutoff Boltzmann equation's solution into a Fourier series in spatial variables, with coefficients satisfying a family of linear integral equations parameterized by the wavenumber. By analyzing these equations, we uncover two distinct time-scales: rapidly decaying modes for high frequencies and a slower decay for low frequencies, ultimately leading to the well-known $1/\tau$ rate for large times. This approach combines discrete sums over frequencies with continuous integrals to estimate solutions, a technique novel to non-localization kinetic theory and offeran alternative to existing methods like Wigner transforms.

This study develops a statistical model for wave height and direction probabilities in a given wind speed, utilizing a non-Gaussian random field that aligns with observed data. The theoretical predictions of this model match a physical model's results, which models the surface as white caps and breaking waves under various wind conditions. Key parameters of this physical model are the group velocity ratio, which varies from 0.6 to 0.8, and the parameter $f_{g}$, which can range widely depending on wind conditions. Notably, stronger winds lead to greater asymmetry in wave slope distributions, with implications for wave steepness and the ratio of group velocity to phase velocity in limited data scenarios.

The management of changes in software systems, referred to as bug fixing, can be effectively handled by leveraging singular value decomposition. A framework has been developed to illustrate this concept, utilizing historical software data from the Mozilla Firefox repository to simulate and analyze bug fixing processes. By applying linear regression models and subsequent dimension reduction, these models predicted bug fixing outcomes with notable accuracy, matching observed actual values.

Social media platforms, such as Twitter, play a crucial role in spreading news, opinions, and emotions during a crisis like the COVID-19 pandemic. To effectively manage this pandemic, it's essential to gain insight into the opinions being voiced on Twitter. Although several studies have sought to classify sentiments from tweets, the current approaches lack consideration for the dynamic evolution of sentiments over time. This research proposes a novel semi-supervised deep learning framework, based on dynamic time-series learning, within a cohesive time-series framework. This framework not only captures the dynamic nature of sentiments over time through dynamic embeddings, but also integrates dynamic temporal dependencies. It offers a unified approach for time-series sentiment analysis, enabling accurate time-series classification and time-series sentiment labeling. We validate our method using public datasets, showcasing superior performance on both time-series classification and time-series sentiment labeling tasks. Our code is available online at the specified GitHub repository.

In the context of the BCS-BCSL theory, we've developed a novel expression for the critical temperature $T_c$ of superconducting transitions in layered materials, applicable to a wide range of such materials. By examining experimental phonon dispersion data, we calculated the average intralayer and interlayer coupling energies, finding the intralayer energy to be significantly larger, on the order of $100\text{K}$ to $1000\text{K}$, surpassing both the interlayer energy and $T_c$ itself. The classic BCS-BCSL theory fails to account for this observation. We propose an alternative form of the critical temperature equation, akin to the Ginzburg-Landau theory, which we believe can more accurately represent the physics of cuprate superconductors, along with providing a new expression for the interlayer coupling energy in terms of magnetic flux penetration length and intralayer energy gap.

A quark star may undergo a phase transition from interacting quarks to deconfined quark-gluon plasma, significantly altering its properties.  We employ the formalism of quantum field theory in finite temperature and density to derive the equation of state for this phase, utilizing the one-loop approximation and the Su(3) group, to study its impact on the star's behavior.  Initially, we consider ideal quarks and gluons, subject to the SU(3) symmetry, and later incorporate the influence of color interactions via the strong force.  Analyzing the equation of state in both ultrarelativistic and non-relativistic regimes, we observe a shift from proportional to $T^4$ and $T^2$ in the pressure and chemical potential, respectively, to similar proportions with different coefficients upon the introduction of color interactions.  These modifications influence the star's mass-radius, fundamental oscillation frequency, and star pulsations, which can be observed through gravitational waves.

In 1980, Harold Tai introduced the concept of a Tai mapping between two binary unordered trees. Two unordered trees are considered equivalent under the Tai relation if their Tai mappings share the same weight. Notably, Tai equivalence forms a congruence relation on the set of all binary unordered trees and its applications extend to areas like the verification of hardware and protocol systems. Various researchers have explored Tai equivalence across the contexts of expression, process, and circuit equality.

According to a recent study by Zhang and Li in 2018, determining the maximum-weight Tai mapping between two given unordered trees is an NP-hard problem even when restricted to binary unordered trees. However, their analysis left open the question of whether this subproblem belongs to the harder classes of complexity classes like $FP^{NP}$ or $F^{PP}$. We have made two key contributions. First, we have shown that the subproblem of finding a maximum-weight Tai mapping is as complex as the maximum matching problem in general graphs, and thus has the same computational hardness. This also implies that the same level of difficulty applies to finding a maximum-weight anti Tai mapping between two given unordered trees. As a result, both problems can be solved using a polynomial number of queries to an NP oracle. Second, we have developed an algorithm with a single-query solution for both problems. This involves utilizing a modified version of the ellipsoid algorithm combined with a polynomial-number alternative method, requiring only a single query to an $F^{

The compass state, which has a high Loschmidt rate of decay and a similar phase transition as the phase diagram, is analyzed using a new framework that links time and space through the concept of entanglement. Researchers found that the compass state's variance is mainly determined by a few modes and is resistant to decoherence. Furthermore, dephasing causes only minor changes to the reduced density matrix and leads to a new phase, which can be estimated with high accuracy even under noisy conditions. Furthermore, the study discovers that mean squared errors exhibit a sudden shift, which is associated with a multi-critical point in time-spacetime diagram. Researchers used quantum dynamics to define a new type of phase, which is resistant to dephasing and is linked to the compass state's phase, and found that estimating damping parameters in metrology is highly influenced by the variance of dominant modes in the compass state.

A comprehensive numerical model of a protoplanetary disk's thermal structure has been developed, accounting for various cooling mechanisms, the interaction between radiation and matter, and the effects of radial transport. This detailed model captures the complexity of a protoplanetary disk's temperature profile, which exhibits distinct behaviors in different regions due to varying dust distribution and radiation-dust interaction. Consequently, the disk displays inefficient cooling in its outer regions, a sudden cooling transition at the Helium line, and a change in the temperature behavior in its inner regions. Our results also show that two-dimensional numerical models that assume uniform temperature distribution along the vertical axis of the disk are insufficient for accurately representing the temperature and dust distribution in its different regions. This underscores the importance of considering one-dimensional numerical models that incorporate dust distribution and radiation-matter interaction to accurately model the disk's physical and chemical evolution, including the formation of the Sun.

This note explores the behavior of harmonic functions that split off from shrinking Ricci solitons. We demonstrate that for parabolic endomorphisms on a manifold of dimension $m$, harmonic functions with specific growth limitations have bounded dimensionality. Furthermore, this has an impact on the structure of the base of the soliton when it contains a non-properly linear growth harmonic function. Notably, the Euclidean space is uniquely identified as the only complete non-compact complete flat strip under these conditions.

A significant challenge exists in putting dynamic backdoor attacks into practice
across various classification tasks. The attack must remain subtle for clean
input data while being triggered effectively with a relatively small
proportion of poisoned input. Building upon the concept of a stochastic backdoor,
this research proposes an innovative method called Random Multi-Target Backdoor
that is easy to execute, robust against various defensive techniques, and with
a reduced poison ratio, yields higher triggering accuracy. Moreover, this study
also develops two additional strategies to mitigate defense techniques such as
adversarial defense and pruning, quickly enabling the backdoor when activated.

In the US Geodetic Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI) Observational Network (ONC) 2019-2020 analysis, our team discovered that parallax effects significantly hindered the precision of our observations. To overcome this challenge, we modified the standard analysis software by incorporating an extra parameter that accounted for parallax's varying impact based on a planet's position in the solar system. By breaking this effect down into its constituent parts, we discovered that it largely depends on a planet's position above the ecliptic plane, which in turn explains the previously observed ONC network bias in ecliptic latitude parallax shift. To further minimize this parallax influence, we determined that sites in high latitudinal regions should observe quasar pairs with large differences in declination, whereas sites in lower latitudinal regions should do so in terms of latitude.

This research extends four algebraic model reduction techniques from nonlinear oscillatory systems with multiple degrees of freedom to nonlinear gyroscopic systems that also incorporate damping. By leveraging the combined invariance of the gyroscopic and damping properties, relationships between their kernels and column spaces can be exploited to simplify existing algorithmic frameworks. The reductions enable elimination of both gyroscopic and damping components, as well as scenarios where both are present, within their respective system structures. The streamlined algorithms demonstrate significant efficiency improvements, achieving at least one order of magnitude faster performance with reduced computational complexities.

We've created a stable type II dyon in two types of interacting Bose-Einstein condensates using the method of balance between nonlinearity and dispersion. By accounting for mean-field and quantum fluctuations, we determined the stable sizes of this type II dyon and observed that it consists of two opposing solitons. When an external magnetic field is applied, the type II dyon breaks apart into individual solitons, and there's a critical point where it transforms into type I dyons. Type I dyons have the same sign of solitons and are more resistant to external magnetic fields, causing their core density to increase and the width of the outer tail to decrease. Furthermore, a binary Bose-Einstein condensate with solitons of varying masses exhibits asymmetry in density distribution and presents a larger transition range from type II to type I dyons. Notably, when solitons with positive and negative masses interact, they create a large density-free area, and an even stronger magnetic field can cause the type II dyon to transform into two separate solitons.

We introduce a novel encoding technique for homomorphic parallel computation,
which modifies the traditional encoding to represent entire Computed Field
Vectors (CFOs) in a way that supports efficient processing of multiple
integers simultaneously through packed operations on homomorphic parameters.
This new encoding technique builds upon existing techniques, including BGV,
TFHE, and CKKS, and enables the creation of a sophisticated coding scheme
capable of handling complex, nested programs for secure machine learning
inferencing.
By incorporating this new encoding, we integrate it into the SecureCloud
platform for CKKS-based secure computation, which allows the processing of
multiple integers at once, leading to considerable improvements in performance
and a reduction in runtime by up to 10 times for practical ML inference
programs, with only minimal overhead in other operations, according to our
benchmarks, which consider both pure and mixed computation scenarios, and
demonstrate the effectiveness of this technique in real-world applications.

Researchers utilized data from the HI Legacy Survey to discover eight additional HI clouds near Milky Way and Andromeda, adding to previously known 34 clouds. These cloud complexes exist within a distinct population occupying a gap in the phase-space diagram, indicating they form a separate group from galaxies. Furthermore, these HI clouds occupy a crucial spatial region between the Local Group and other nearby galaxy groups. The largest of these clouds, labeled HLX-1, contains more mass than and is 10 times larger than the HI cloud surrounding the Sagittarius Dwarf Galaxy. HLX-1 is currently approaching at a significant speed, which could lead to an interaction with the Milky Way within the coming decades. The discovery implies that these cloud complexes may play an essential role in localizing and characterizing nearby galaxy interactions within the Milky Way-Andromeda system before their eventual collision in the future.

This work introduces an innovative approach to constructing question answering systems by leveraging a limited set of pre-defined, semantic-rich questions and answers. Taking a top-down, hierarchical view, we identify key elements of the given dataset, ensuring each component leads to more detailed sub-elements. We employ a versatile, generic framework that utilizes representation learning and logical labels to learn from the provided data. Each question and answer in the system is linked to its respective logical label. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method by applying it to three distinct datasets, achieving top performance in the leading Chinese Question Answering benchmark, performed by our model, Multi-ANSI, on the CMRC 2018 platform.

We've compiled comprehensive experimental electronic spectra for the ScO+ cation, and our findings pose a challenge to existing theoretical models. Although several groups have attempted to full-spectrally model small molecular cations, the task remains uncompleted. To do so would require theoretical results to match the extensive, manually compiled experimental spectra. Given the lack of prior theoretical works that can match our experimental findings for ScO+, there's an opportunity for a thorough, full-spectral theoretical analysis.

We provide a detailed algorithm that can break down the sum of two squares theorem, as well as its counterpart for quadratic forms, into two distinct parts: first identifying the necessary coefficients, and second verifying those coefficients within a given field of rational numbers. Our method, which is based on a classic algorithm for rational factorization by Salomonson, is designed for explicit algebraic extensions, including those involving the root of a polynomial with rational coefficients. We will demonstrate the algorithm through multiple examples, including the decomposition of a complicated form that does not divide as the product of two simpler forms.

By combining fast-time scale data from X-ray sensors on satellite platforms with wider-field data from space telescopes, we've obtained a robust measurement of the measured correlation lag for a black hole's disc. This measurement, along with its accompanying uncertainty, is distinct from the positive lag previously observed on a similar object, thus resolving the previously conflicting results. The measured correlation lag, if utilized, can aid in future observations by providing a tool to automatically identify gravitational wave mergers.

As relational machine learning models gain more attention, it's crucial to
establish guidelines for benchmarking their performance. We outline our
experience in evaluating the effectiveness of relational machine learning
approaches in a pharmacology setting, where the goal is to identify drugs
that may have therapeutic effects or avoid adverse effects in patients affected
by various diseases. We formulated a series of challenges involving three
different datasets and invited researchers to submit a range of relational
machine learning models for evaluation. We discuss the important considerations
when assessing relational machine learning models' performance and present
empirical data on the performance of various models, including state-of-the-art
relational machine learning approaches. We also explored the potential for
using relational machine learning in this field and outlined several areas for
future work.

This email aims to provide a simpler proof of a result obtained by Lejay and Gubler concerning the Young integral. Specifically, we will demonstrate that if $f$ and $y$ are bounded functions from the real line to the real line, with $f$ belonging to the Hölder continuous functions of order $\alpha$ and $y$ belonging to the Hölder continuous functions of order $\beta$, where the sum of $\alpha$ and $\beta$ is greater than one, then the Young integral is well-defined and equals a limit that involves the average of the product of $f$ and $y$ over small intervals, as the interval size approaches zero.

A random walk that alternates between model training updates and shifts into a training area with a modified step size is proposed. This dynamic is designed to balance communication and computation over time, achieving a optimal ratio. The approach is resilient to network problems as it locally adjusts computation to model age, avoiding the need for synchronized computations. It also reduces computation during periods of extended model propagation. This study examines how this method performs in distributed settings, with a focus on its convergence properties in a stochastic image recognition task, with promising empirical results demonstrating its effectiveness.

Fluid dynamics in rotating conditions exhibit intricate turbulence that is currently being investigated through direct numerical simulations. These simulations demonstrate that inertial wave turbulence conforms to a $E(\epsilon_{\omega})\propto\omega^{-2}\frac{B^{3}}{\omega^{5}}$ spectrum, identified by Galtier in 2001, with $\omega$ denoting the magnitude of the wave vector, $\epsilon_{\omega}$ denoting the energy influx spectrum, and $B$ denoting a constant depending on the rate of wave vector rotation. Furthermore, our研究表明, the turbulent energy dissipation can be idenitified as $\epsilon_{\omega}\theta_{\omega}(1-\omega^{2}\theta_{\omega})$, with $\theta_{\omega}$ denoting the ratio between enstrophy and mean magnetic field squared, $B^{2}$. Our findings indicate that $\omega$ exhibits a decrease as $\omega\propto\omega_{min}^{2}/\omega_{max}$, with $\omega_{min}$ and $\omega_{max}$ denoting, respectively, the minimum and maximum scales at which energy enters and enstrophy enters, thereby supporting the notion that magnetic effects dominate at small scales and that wave turbulence persists.

Investigating the impact of receiving mental health treatment on reoffending rates, as well as the severity and frequency of reoffenses among individuals with psychiatric disorders, we utilized an innovative analytical approach known as multi-event analysis on comprehensive, population-wide data from all 50 US states over a ten-year period. Mental health treatment information was obtained直接从州级数据中的所有 50 个美国州 over a ten-year 时期 from 2004 年至 2013 年. Our findings reveal that those who received treatment had lower reoffending rates compared to untreated individuals for various crime categories including burglary, fraud, production of counterfeit goods, arson. Moreover, treated patients exhibited reduced reoffenses with more serious classifications and increased frequency of reoffending among those who did reoffend for drug-related crimes. This study is groundbreaking as it is, to our knowledge, the first to analyze mental health treatment's effect on crime rates within complete, state-wide populations using officially registered criminal records. We utilized an advanced statistical method called multi-event analysis, which is particularly well-suited for examining time-dependent events within longitudinal datasets.

This paper addresses the challenge of balancing diverse medical image styles while training segmentation models, and introduces an innovative method called interpolation-based mixing to handle this issue. Unlike traditional approaches, interpolation-based mixing creates seamless transitions between images of different styles, resulting in better model performance and consistent, high-quality segmentations. To further enhance learning capabilities, this method leverages semi-supervised techniques by enforcing consistency in segmentations along the interpolation paths, and also incorporates intensity preservation to maintain the natural appearance of mixed images. The proposed method's superiority over current state-of-the-art models is demonstrated through comprehensive experiments on three distinct segmentation tasks.

This note outlines the potential of the Forward Detector (JETFEX) at the LHC, with the capability to process up to $10^{10}$ collisions per second, for possible contribution to forward physics research mandated by the LHC Upgrade. To the best of our knowledge, the JETFEX design has not been previously developed, but we illustrate its suitability for this critical research area. If the LHC Upgrade proceeds, we propose that the FETFEX device, capable of executing intricate analyses at this unprecedented speed, could directly influence specific experiments and contribute to their operational efficiency.

Recent advancements in 3D image rendering have emerged from the success of
Unsupervised Articulated Body Rendering (UABR) training framework.  Although UABR
achieves impressive results, its reliance on one-to-one correspondence between
corresponding images and the need for corresponding views of an object's
configuration restrict its usage to objects with repetitive symmetries and simple
structures.  To overcome these limitations, we introduce a novel rendering
framework, Continuous Unsupervised Articulated Body Rendering (CUABR), based on
Unsupervised Neural Rendering (UNR) and Unsupervised Depth Configuration Render
(UDCR) modules.  UNR efficiently generates high-fidelity views of object across
different angles and configurations, while UDCR utilizes depth configurations to
rendering unseen object configurations by inferring their corresponding depth
configurations.  Experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed UNR
and UDCR modules, as well as the overall CUABR framework, in experiments on menus,
guitars, and chairs.

Advanced graph neural network methods have successfully quantified local atomic environments in materials by leveraging symmetry-adapted expansions and correlation functions. These features have proven effective in predicting properties such as bond angles and interatomic distances. However, current approaches fall short in capturing the essential information needed to predict electronic structure and other complex properties. They also lack consistency across different coordinate systems and degrees of atomic displacement. To address these limitations, we developed a new feature extractor that draws on invariant polynomials to simultaneously capture interatomic distances and angles in a manner that maintains consistency under rotational transformations of the atomic cluster. This new feature extractor has been shown capable of matching or surpassing the performance of existing models in predicting band structures and total energies from ab initio calculations, particularly for silicon clusters. When applied to disordered systems and nanomaterials, our feature extractor has been found capable of capturing significant local structural features while exhibiting greater efficiency compared to full-volume density functional theory calculations.

This paper examines the conditions under which weak convergence occurs in a specific statistical model, particularly those affecting estimates of functions of the parameter $\theta$ in the distribution function $F_\theta$. Conditions under which consistent estimation via the maximum likelihood method occurs in this model, as well as those under which the maximum likelihood estimator achieves the optimal rate of convergence as defined by the Cramér-Rao lower bound, are investigated. Conditions under which estimation using the method of maximum likelihood falls into categories (A) and (B) are also discussed.

Despite significant advancements in deep learning solutions to the knowledge tracing problem, evaluating these approaches proves to be a challenging task. Existing assessments often rely on flawed, coincidental indicators, hindering the development of precise predictions. To address this issue, we propose a novel evaluation metric based on the core objective of knowledge tracing, which is ascertaining a student's ability to answer a question without knowing their previous quiz answers. We also identify and discuss the shortcomings of current knowledge tracing datasets, then present a comprehensive analysis of state-of-the-art deep learning models, Re-GRU, and k-GRU. Our findings reveal that these models, when applied to certain datasets, perform poorly, tend to memorize existing data, and demonstrate generalized ability to some extent. Ultimately, our study provides a critical examination of current knowledge tracing solutions and offers valuable insights for future research in this field.

This work extends the notion of surjectivity for second-order elliptic differential operators on smooth functions over a smooth manifold without a specified metric. Building on existing concepts of elliptic operators and their associated forms, we develop a broader framework that encompasses a significant class of operators defined on smooth functions. This framework includes important examples, such as Laplace-type operators and Carré du champ operators. We demonstrate that this expanded class of operators preserves key properties, notably the surjectivity and index zero characteristics, which were initially established for standard elliptic operators.

The veriT proof format has significantly advanced since its initial presentation 
at the PxTP workshop in 2010, allowing for highly detailed analysis of 
satisfying models by providing access to the full decision process. 
In 2019, the format saw further improvement with the introduction of 
compressed proofs, which utilize less storage while maintaining the ability 
for in-depth examination of satisfying models. This study first outlines the 
structure of compressed proofs and then compares their efficiency to standard 
formats, revealing that veriT's compressed format offers substantial 
advantages in terms of both storage size and processing time.

This paper introduces a new framework for federated learning, combining the capabilities of aggregating updates from diverse sources and broadcasting enhanced models efficiently.  Analytically, we determine the optimal number of updates to aggregate and the ideal number of devices to broadcast to, ensuring convergence to an optimal solution.  To from a diverse range of model updates, FedBuff introduces a novel method of combining gradient updates, and shows that this method can be analyzed as a stochastic process, and that it results in reduced variance and faster mean convergence.  The proposed framework is theoretically proven to achieve a convergence rate of \($O(1/k)\) for optimization iterations, and the FedBuff algorithm is also shown to converge to a optimal solution.  To demonstrate the effectiveness of FedBuff, we introduce a variant of FedAvg that utilizes the FedBuff framework, and compare it to the original algorithm.  Our results show that FedBuff can significantly enhance the FedAvg's scalability and performance, while maintaining privacy.

This paper explores transfer learning in speech recognition across different language pairs. Our experiments indicate that knowledge transfer from one language to another can yield significant improvements, particularly in less similar languages. To investigate this phenomenon, we utilized the Librispeech dataset and conducted studies across different groups of English, Germanic (consisting of German and Danish subsets), and Polish languages. By analyzing changes in model capacity and regularization strength, we gained valuable insights into how transfer learning affects network behavior. Specifically, we observed that increasing library size enhances the regularization effect, thereby preventing overfitting. Furthermore, our study on network responses to test inputs revealed that transferred knowledge aids in generalizing speech patterns.

To assess novel node embedding methods, we adapted the traditional k-Nearest Neighbors (kNN) classification algorithm for network nodes. Our approach, called "node classification," leverages induced low-dimensional vectors to classify neighboring nodes. We developed a standard test to evaluate and compare different embedding algorithms, which we openly provide, along with results for various algorithms, in Supplementary Materials on GitHub. Our evaluation metric measures the embedding algorithm's performance relative to an optimal classifier with unlimited knowledge of the network structure. We enhanced the kNN baseline using a smart feature selection technique, and our findings show that several new algorithms, including PRADE and GENRE, outperform the kNN baseline, as confirmed by statistical tests.

A study of the $B^+$ decay into two $K_S$ mesons and a $K^+$ meson at LHCb reveals distinct structures in the energy spectrum of the $K_S K_S$ pair. Using an amplitude analysis, researchers found that a scalar ($S$-wave) contribution explains the broad feature around 1 GeV/$c^2$. Employing the Bessel function method for unbinned maximum likelihood estimation, the study determined the $S$-wave contribution's parameters, including its end point parameters and phase space factors. As a result, a more precise determination of the fragmentation variable $f_0(m_{K_S K_S})$ was achieved with reduced uncertainty.

We resolve the long-standing uncertainty in primordial black hole (PBH) mass ranges that could constitute all dark matter, utilizing latest Planck and WMAP observations as well as gravitational wave data from the LIGO/Virgo collaborations. By incorporating both direct and indirect constraints from the 13-TeV ATLAS and CMS experiments, a comprehensive six-panel diagram is produced with regulated dark matter mass windows for each of the considered mechanisms. Currently five separate mass windows remain, though most correspond to negligible in the order of $10^{-8}$ kg primordial black holes due to their inconsistency with unitarity final states in gamma-ray scattering events. Advanced unitarity final state considerations at lower masses than previously thought unitarily insecure, namely down to sigma~0.15 nb for 8 TeV LHC data, could expand these small mass windows significantly, potentially increasing them to millions of tons. Furthermore recent predictions of quasi-primitive black holes with masses mirroring that of the ATLAS missing transverse energy events, offer another unique opportunity to detect and differentiate primordial from microscopic primordial black holes.

Series elastic actuatures (SEAs) utilize a flexible component to smooth out force discrepancies between an actuator and load, making them highly effective for interacting with both people and objects. Although precise force measurement is crucial for these applications, accurately measuring the force in the elastic component can be challenging. This study introduces a novel filtering algorithm, tailored specifically to the nonlinear characteristics and noise sources affecting force measurement, including the nonlinearity of the sensing element and the sensor's inaccuracy. Unlike traditional methods like Lorentz transformation, this customized algorithm addresses the limitations of these approaches. Experimental results demonstrate that the new method significantly outperforms existing algorithms in measuring force accuracy. Furthermore, comparisons with real-world force measurements indicate that without implementing this algorithm, accurate force measurement becomes unattainable, particularly under high-load conditions. However, with the proposed filtering technique, not only is accurate force measurement achievable, but also reduces the measurement error in low-load conditions from as much as 45.5 N to as little as 1.03 N.

As colonies develop, they often break apart into smaller units due to competition for resources, a phenomenon observed in various species across different habitats. To understand the underlying mechanisms driving the colony size during early stages of social entity formation, we created a model that combines an agent-based model with a statistical analysis. The agent-based model simulates the interactions between individual members and their environment, while the statistical analysis helps interpret the complex dynamics. The specific system we studied involves the self-organization of two-dimensional particle assemblies. These assemblies are separated by flowing liquids, which either increase or decrease the colony size through a feedback mechanism. The simulation results and statistical analysis reveal that the colony structure is influenced by the balance between fluid expansion and particle re-aggregation, leading to a pattern of nested or separate entities. Furthermore, our model predicts a scale at which the colony fragments stabilize, a scale determined by the interaction between adjacent rifts, and it is shown that this scale can be explained by an balance between the rate of particle aggregation and the expansion of the fluid, and it also considers how this balance affects the distance between adjacent cracks in the raft and changes in the raft's perimeter can cause variations in the colony structure.

We investigate the renormalization group flow in a multi-component complex scalar field on a cubic lattice, identifying distinct regions corresponding to relevant, marginal, and irrelevant flows. By mapping between lattice models and continuum field theories, we establish a connection that allows us to observe a theoretical RG fixed point - where the flow is marginal - as a boundary separating regions of stable and unstable equilibrium. Additionally, we demonstrate that this boundary exhibits a moving singularity in its location, depending on the magnitude of mass differences between field components. Finally, we propose an experimental approach using ultracold atoms to test different flow regimes and visualize the boundary's behavior.

For the effective management of autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs), we need decision-making methods capable of swiftly processing vast amounts of data within short timeframes. Our primary objective is to enhance the policy evaluation process for underwater navigation tasks when using model-based reinforcement learning, which can involve creating and evaluating numerous models in different states and taking multiple actions, potentially requiring numerous simulations for accuracy. To achieve this, we developed a novel algorithm called SPGP-SARSA, inspired by the SPGP algorithm and the SARSA algorithm, which utilizes real-world simulations to derive the policy and value functions, thereby reducing or eliminating the need for additional Monte Carlo simulations. To test the efficiency and precision of our algorithm, we conducted experiments on underwater navigation problems of various sizes, which involved multiple AUV models, resulting in significant reductions in computation time while maintaining a comparable level of accuracy to the original SPGP algorithm.

We've established that the smallest comparators needed for sorting networks to function, at specific depths, are as follows: for depth 1 and 2, it's 2 and 4 respectively; additionally we know from existing research that at depth 3 it's 6 and likely 5 comparators are sufficient. Surprisingly, our findings indicate a different pattern emerges as the depth passes 4, where the minimal arity does not consistently increase with each additional comparison layer.

Building upon a previous study, we have constructed a range of new solutions for a relativistic stellar model consisting of two distinct fluids, where the second fluid's density is directly proportional to the square of the first fluid's density. By utilizing the method of fluid decomposition, we can obtain solutions for this two-fluid model from a one-fluid precursor, under the condition that the corresponding one-fluid solution adheres to a specific mathematical relationship. This construction allows us to generate multiple stellar models using well-established one-fluid solutions as a basis. We have specifically analyzed the physical characteristics of several two-fluid models based on their geometric deformation properties, including adiabatic indices, and found that they comply with the causality principle. It was also determined that these models exhibit type B behavior according to Barraco's classification.

We employed a scale-length parameter to define the density distribution in a grand design spiral galaxy model, spanning from short to long scale lengths. Using N-body simulations, we analyzed bars in the galaxy and found that its size significantly impacts bar formation. In cases of short scale lengths, bars are prominent, whereas bars become less formed or absent in cases of long scale lengths. A sudden shift in bar characteristics occurs at an intermediate value, indicating that bar formation is highly influenced by the density distribution scale length. In addition, we found that the critical angular radius for bar formation corresponds to the transition in bar characteristics and is consistent with observations of ring and bar formation in starburst galaxies.

The impact of magnetic fields on the formation of merger remnant galaxies following gas-rich major mergers is investigated in this study. Using three-dimensional large N-body and radiative hydrodynamics simulations, we examined the effects of magnetic fields on the formation of spiral galaxies resulting from the merger of two massive gas-rich galaxies. Our results indicate that while the global mass assembly is largely unaffected by magnetic fields, they do play a significant role in shaping local mass assembly and global gas dynamics. Specifically, we found that the accumulation of potential energy through the compression of magnetic field lines results in increased local temperatures. Furthermore, the dynamics of the merger are largely shaped by the flow of angular momentum, which in turn affects the amount of material that can cross the central region. While magnetic fields have a negligible effect on the inner regions, they do significantly impact the outer regions of the disk, where they regulate the amount of material that can accumulate and influence the development of spiral arms. Ultimately, our results demonstrate that the presence of magnetic fields can have a profound effect on the morphology of merger remnant galaxies, with or without a central supermassive black hole.

This research outlines a novel network, the 3D Contrastive Mixup Classification network, that leverages 3D convolution layers to classify medical CT scan slices into three pandemic severity categories. Unlike traditional balanced classification methods, it specifically addresses real-world scenarios with unbalanced data distributions.

We introduce two distinctive components to our network. Firstly, it employs contrastive learning to effectively distinguish between similar and dissimilar data points. Secondly, it employs ordered pick up-sampling to maintain spatial and channel-wise information during the down-sampling process.

To validate our approach, we utilized a comprehensive dataset consisting of 9,666 COVID-19 and 10,958 non-COVID-19 CT scan slices, which was then used to train, validate, and test our proposed network, as well as other competing methods. Our results outperform existing approaches and demonstrate that our proposed network exhibits exceptional robustness and reliability.

Research into spelling correction using neural networks has produced notable outcomes; however, using general purpose models to fix spelling in specific domain texts remains limited. Traditional transfer learning techniques for domain adaptation typically involve training domain-specific models from scratch, which incures high costs. In contrast, our proposed method enables an efficient fine-tuning of a comprehensive grammar model on particular domain datasets, requiring minimal resources. We demonstrate the efficacy of this domain-specific fine-tuning approach by comparing it to conventional multi-task transfer learning methods, yielding superior results in overall domain spelling correction.

During the COVID-19 emergency, a concerning 200% increase in U.S. suicide rates was observed following the March 13, 2020 announcement of a rounding rule for small geographic areas by the CDC. To evaluate whether this policy change influenced those statistics, a statistical model was developed to assess the data's behavior. The study's results indicate that before adopting the new policy, there was typically no detectable bias in estimating suicide rates after adjusting for measurement errors inherent in small datasets. However, the results show that after implementing the new policy, adjusted estimates exhibited significant upward biases, with some states experiencing estimates that were overestimated by as much as 200%. Given that aggregated data across all 50 states yielded accurate, unbiased estimates with minimal standard errors, researchers concluded that rounding likely obscured important subnational findings during the COVID-19 epidemic. Therefore, further investigation into the relationship between reported CDC data and adjusted data across all 50 states is crucial for better understanding this phenomenon.

We investigate the magnetic properties of GdInO$_3$ single-crystal samples using a combination of 199Gd M$\beta$N measurements, first-principles calculations, and conventional neutron diffraction. $\text{Gd}^{3+}$ ions in $\text{GdInO}_3$ are arranged in a rock-salt lattice and connected via corner-shared $\text{InO}_6$ octahedra, which we analyze using an effective spin Hamiltonian to understand long-range magnetic ordering. $\text{GdInO}_3$ exhibits a cubic structure with the space group $pgm$ and a lattice parameter of $a = 11.6499(4)$ Å. The M$\beta$N technique provides vital local magnetic information, initially indicating the direction and strength of the internal magnetic field at the Gd nuclei, as well as modifications to the InO$_6$ electric field gradient resulting from the presence of $\text{Gd}^{3+}$ ions. The results indicate a 0.24(5) MHz reduction in the EFG at a site without Gd neighbors, while the EFG at neighboring sites experiences a 2.6(5) MHz increase. Our analysis also shows that all $\text{Gd}^{3+}$ nuclei exhibit nearly identical hyperfine interactions, regardless of their local crystal environment, thus confirming the validity of the effective spin Hamiltonian

The round-robin protocol for the cut-and-choose algorithm is analyzed with a different objective function compared to its conventional use, focusing on an iterative process that ensures a fair allocation among players with divergent valuation functions. By incorporating local swap rules, a new round-robin approach is developed, offering strong fairness guarantees similar to those of the standard round-robin protocol but with less computational complexity. This new approach ensures each player's allocation can be at least as valuable to them as any other player, and the allocated items form a matching. Further variations, including the use of a broader class of swap rules and a modified version without requiring new items, are explored. Different round-robin versions are analyzed and compared, and their relationships to alternative algorithms like the young's rule are examined.

This paper addresses the challenge of acquiring labels for target data. A novel technique is introduced, building upon a detection-based pseudo-labeling framework. This new method involves generating multiple translations of a single Pseudo-label from a variety of target domains. The technique is refined by incorporating an innovative filter, designed to prevent the introduction of noisy labels. Demonstrations via experiments and results show that this approach yields enhanced performance, ultimately yielding larger increases in classification accuracy compared to utilizing sole Pseudo labels.

By upgrading spectroscopic coverage from 880 fibers to 3520 fibers, the expanded survey obtains 1420 new spectra and reanalyzes all existing spectra in the galaxy's interaction region. The sensitivity of future paleo-detectors for dark matter near the 1 GeV mass threshold could extend into new parameter space that's unaffected by constraints from nuclear-recoil experiments. We investigate this unique area by examining the implications of existing paleo-detector limits in conjunction with constraints derived from various other experiments. Furthermore, we assess the potential of finding anomalous isotopic ratios in ancient detrital rocks as a result of interactions between low-mass dark matter particles and nucleons, which would serve a dual purpose: providing evidence for the existence of this phenomenon and calibrating the required detection sensitivity to realize this potential. Such a sensitivity, as indicated by models, could be achieved with missions like MASTODON using a suitable sample of ~100 grams of 87Sr over a million years.

Modern databases, capturing complex transaction histories, reflect the intricate relationships between different data aspects. Retaining all historical data alterations within each transaction can reveal personal details about other users embedded in the data's history. To mitigate this data leakage, we develop a comprehensive model, incorporating both query and update operations, underpinning our framework for assessing both summary and historical data protections based on differential privacy principles. Utilizing techniques from linear systems theory, we analyze the system's dynamics to design efficient differential privacy algorithms, balancing multiple costs in our model to find optimal solutions via closed-form formulas. These solutions reveal pivotal insights, particularly demonstrating how storing data updates in differential privacy complies with querying the system also protected by differential privacy.

Recent advances in machine learning have led to the development of highly complex models, but these achievements come with increased interpretability challenges. Using Constraint Programming, we propose an efficient framework for feature interpretability that leverages Minimal Unsatisfiable Cores to identify and understand irrelevant features in classification tasks. By minimizing the sum of thresholds of unused features, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through comparisons with established methods on standard classification datasets, utilizing Mixed Integer Linear Programming solvers.

This research focuses on developing an automated system for segmenting surgical instruments used during laparoscopic surgery. We propose a novel deep learning approach, the Dual decoder attention network (DDANet), which enhances traditional encoding-decoding frameworks by refining feature maps through attention mechanisms in two-decoder skip connections. Our method leverages multiple恩eural networks to capture both contextual and fine-grained instrument details. By incorporating context and fine information from separate branches and fusing them through additional deconvolution layers, DDANet outperforms other state-of-the-art surgical segmentation techniques. Furthermore, our model exhibits enhanced robustness to variations in surgical scenes, instrument types, and numbers, when tested on the CholecSeG dataset.

This work proposes a novel unsupervised ReID framework that integrates
a contrastive learning pre-training phase to generate discriminative feature
representations. Our approach, in which objects are treated as distinct
classes for contrastive learning, is called UnsuFrame. This pre-training step
is followed by two methods for transferring the learned representation from the
source domain to the target domain. Our experiments on multiple real-world multi-domain ReID benchmarks, involving single, multi-sensor and domain adaptation scenarios, demonstrate the efficacy of UnsuFrame, achieving particularly impressive results in the challenging domain adaptation task and surpassing the current state-of-the-art unsupervised ReID performance. All experimental codes will be publicly available.

We develop a novel framework for predicting value-at-risk that incorporates growth models, which serves as an alternative to the widely-used GARCH framework. Our proposed method utilizes an innovative information measure to construct a GARCH-type model specifically designed for value-at-risk forecasting, and shows promising results in experimenting with Hungarian stock data. Our framework also outperforms the traditional GARCH model and a simple moving average model in a comparative study, with further results presented in this paper.

The study analyzes various sampling algorithms, including Marginalized MultiNest, MultiNest, Dynamical Nested Sampling, and GWCS, to evaluate their effectiveness in exploring pulsar timing array parameter space for the detection of a pulsar gravitational wave signal. By simulating data based on the predicted pulsar timing array data model and adding random noise, researchers were able to compare the results of each sampling algorithm. In comparing the estimated parameters and associated uncertainties of models with embedded signals, all algorithms showed similar performance. However, dynamic nested sampling and GWCS demonstrated greater stability in uncertainty estimation. When analyzing data without an actual signal, multi nest and GWCS struggled with estimating parameters of general relativistic masses due to excessive likelihood peaks, whereas marginalized multi nest and dynamic nested sampling effectively identified and marginalized these peaks. When comparing computational costs, GWCS was found to be significantly faster than the other algorithms, taking less than 10% of the time it took dynamic nested sampling to estimate parameters in simulated data with a signal.

Using the MILC three-flavor lattice QCD data, we derive the partial wave decomposition of hadron masses, such as the pion mass in the s-channel and the sigma term, for the sigma term we also consider the cbs, ud and su channel contributions separately. The results show that the sigma term can be accurately represented by the sum of corresponding lattice QCD channel masses, and our method provides a way to break down the sigma term without relying on the heavy mass limit approximation. Furthermore, our method reveals the influence of quark mass changes on the sigma term's channel composition, which varies from the traditional assumption of 50/50. This research has implications for the accuracy of theoretical predictions in chiral perturbation theory, particularly for analyzing the sigma term's behavior at non-zero lattice momenta.

New high-precision observations of the UV emissions from classical T Tauri star HV 570, acquired by the Cosmic Origins Spectrograph on the James Webb Space Telescope and Hubble Space Telescope, reveal that its accretion rates fluctuate wildly over a one-year period. These extreme variations in accretion rates call into question the reliability of previous conclusions about disk development based on single or limited observations and suggest that mid UV line profiles are deeply influenced by the non-steady-state nature of the accretion flow, at least within the HV 570 system. Our analysis of multi-wavelength data from the Hubble, James Webb, and Kepler telescopes reveals that HV 570's mid infrared spectral energy distribution and X-ray flux remain largely unchanged over the observed year, but its optical and near infrared counterparts exhibit significant variability, with near infrared emissions also reflecting the system's disk structure, contrary to the typical assumption that such emissions originate from long-lived hydrogen lines in the system.

Economic research often uses public opinions as a reference point, yet using the same approach can lead to biased results because people's perceptions of luck's impact on income may differ from its actual effect. This different effect is like a "luck illusion" - where people mistake opportunities for income and can both aid and mislead policymakers. Our research uses a unique survey question to measure this difference in people's understanding of luck's impact on earnings, revealing significant variations in people's views on the distributive system. These differences are not random as they relate to other factors, such as individuals' sense of fairness, as seen in the Adverse Selection Effect. We also observe Adverse Selection in policy support, particularly in people's views on redistribution, which varies based on how they perceive luck's impact, with those who see opportunities affected by luck in favor of redistribution, while those who think income is directly impacted by luck dislike redistribution. This effect of "luck illusion" holds implications for news consumption, campaign contributions, and even organ donation rates.

This study introduces a method for extending stable maps from non-compact symplectic manifolds to a broader category of lax symmetric monoidal varieties, maintaining symmetry. By leveraging this framework, we can define and analyze spaces of stable maps on a torus, which enables us to establish an explicit connection between their Euler characteristics and numerical invariants of a symplectic manifold. These invariants turn out to be a twisted version of the previously described split-locus invariants introduced by J. Solomon. We also demonstrate how a specific case of the on-area-surfaces stable maps category can yield an alternative proof for the equivalence between its Euler characteristic and a topological invariant of a symplectic surface, which was established in our prior research. Additionally, we explore how the Euler characteristics of these surface maps relate to a specific invariant of complex numbers and explore its implications in quantum corrections of topological invariants.

Debugging data pipelines is crucial but often time-consuming, particularly when dealing with large datasets containing minor errors. These errors can originate from various sources, such as past decisions, automated scripts, or human mistakes, and may seem innocuous but can significantly impact the final model's performance. While data scientists have gained the ability to build and maintain complex pipelines, many still find it difficult to efficiently identify errors within these datasets. To tackle this challenge, we introduced DataScope, a data debugger that pinpoints outliers in the input data and propagates their traces to all intermediate outputs and predictions. DataScope achieves high precision in probability estimation for model predictions given an input data point, does this rapidly, and can be integrated into data pipelines as a single inference call. In an iterative process with data scientists, we evaluated DataScope's usability in predicting the location of errors within datasets. Moreover, we demonstrated how DataScope can facilitate targeted data reprocessing, reducing the computation required on large datasets compared to traditional methods.

We employed the Hubble Space Telescope's Wide Field Camera 3 to conduct a deeper analysis of the 121 clusters within the Milky Way's 1Ms Abundance Survey's sample, allowing for a more comprehensive study of the clusters' neutron star radio sources and their counterparts in the radio, radio/infrared, and X-ray spectra. This process added nine previously unidentified sources to the list of 102 within the clusters' cores, bringing the total number of radio sources (including millisecond pulsars and neutron star binaries) to 147. The newly discovered radio sources in the clusters' cores comprise three potential millisecond pulsars, the maximum likelihood estimates of which are more closely aligned with their optical/metric companions, as well as a possibly significant candidate for a neutron star binary in the dwarf galaxy Messier 5. The clusters with the highest densities of radio sources in the core are the ones with the most massive and abundant low-mass black holes, the gravitationally dominant regions are those with higher densities, and the clusters that retain their central density regions are those with specific properties. The gravitational potential of the density regions is influenced by specific factors, and the density regions are located at specific distances from the center of the clusters, where the forces of gravity are balanced against the surrounding forces. Effectively reconstructing hypergraphs from their projection data has significant implications for processing and analyzing large datasets. Unfortunately, the common approach of using an energy minimization framework falls short due to an excessively large solution space. The size of the underlying graph influences the feasibility of this method, necessitating scalable energy functions and innovative graph growth techniques to accommodate existing and new nodes. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel, local algorithm that leverages key statistics of the projections to directly infer hyperedges, along with associated weights, without initial knowledge of the underlying structure. This innovative algorithm enables feasible reconstruction of the underlying hidden structure of a system from its projected observations. We validate its performance through synthetic and real-world datasets, demonstrating the scalability of our energy function and the effectiveness of our graph growth technique, ultimately confirming the accuracy of our edge inference method.

We've developed an innovative model for analyzing directional laser beams, applying it to calculate the directional characteristics of explicitly directed emission models. Our calculations involved evaluating integrals related to laser beam divergence, comparing the results to both implicit and explicit models. Our study revealed that directional beam characteristics differ between the two models and can be quantitatively measured. Additionally, we found that the average divergence angle is directly dependent on the distribution of photon angles in the emitted beam and that this relationship can be expressed as the fourth power of that distribution.

We've developed an analytical approach to predicting the first-time correlation functions for coherent light interacting with systems of atoms. Our methodology is based on a semi-classical model and allows us to derive exact expressions for both first-time and two-time second-order correlation functions across various scenarios. Using our framework, we obtained analytical results for the steady-state first-time correlation functions and 1D spatial intensity correlation measurements. Notably, our results highlight a non-trivial role played by the phase of the incident light on the system's output.

This study offers some initial insights into the application of Shared Individual Trajectories (SIT) as a method for enhancing the learning process in offline multi-agent environments. In this approach, the learning process is broken down into separate value functions, each assessing a singular agent's action based on the combined actions of all agents in the system. Utilizing the principles of Counterfactual Regret Minimization, we develop the SITD algorithm to efficiently enforce consistency across the joint policy while only using data from one agent. We demonstrate through experiments on the Sea Monsters game that the algorithm can successfully learn complex tasks, including those with the use of countering actions, from a single agent's data. Additionally, we show how increasing the number of cooperative agents enhances the algorithm's performance, and that introducing counterfactual data can significantly improve its learning capacity.

This paper presents a novel Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture 
for image registration, leveraging label fields from two input images to align 
corresponding features through contour matching and spatial location correction. 
Our CNN approach combines advantages of intensity-based and contour-based methods, 
resulting in superior performance compared to standard intensity-based methods 
according to our experiments. By incorporating gradient-based optimization into 
the registration process, this model achieves real-world applicability, while 
demonstrating enhanced accuracy over existing benchmark CNN registration models. 
Our proposed approach also shows significant improvements in handling medical 
images, particularly in post-surgical scenarios.

A persistent debate surrounds the notion of multparticle entanglement as a fundamental resource, with some asserting its supremacy and others, like Guarrera and Stella, demonstrating that conventional measures of multparticle entanglement can be reduced to sums of pairwise interactions, rendering them redundant. This discussion is further complicated by the existence of states exhibiting nonlocal correlations and quantum steering beyond the capacity of bipartite entangled states. Notably, we discover that a singular particle can generate nonlocal effects and induce states of entangment among multiple observers, a phenomenon that relies on the capacity for that particle to interact with several separated systems simultaneously through a globally encompassing field. This is demonstrated using spin interactions and can also be achieved with massless particles possessing at least a quadrupole momentum, providing a practical pathway for creating states of entangment and facilitating the examination of the boundary between classical and quantum realms.

Next-generation Internet of Vehicles (IoVs) will offer unparalleled convenience and mobility, yet simultaneously increase vulnerability to privacy breaches and criminal activities. To tackle these challenges, IoVs will employ advanced authentication techniques, including Cryptography and Blockchain technologies. This paper delves into the integration of Blockchain in IoV systems, exploring its capabilities to secure data, ensure its integrity, and provide tracing functionality. Building on existing research, this study proposes a novel decentralized IoV framework based on Blockchain, offering enhanced security and reliability for shared data. It outlines the operational process of the proposed system and analyzes its performance through simulation, demonstrating significant improvements in security and average confirmation time compared to existing solutions.

V392 Persei, a intermediate high mass X-ray binary with an accreting white dwarf, has been under study since its S-class nova eruption in 2015. Observations of the system's UV and X-ray emissions during its 2017 outburst enabled us to investigate the long-term accretion state evolution following the nova eruption. The system displayed an intermediate high state with an super-soft X-ray emission lasting from July to November 2017, indicating the presence of a thick, turbulent nova debris disk. The outer disk regions allowed high energy X-rays to pass through, resulting in an observed power spectrum with an amplitudes of less than 10 percent. The system switched to a dimmer, harsher disk state in November 2017, marking the transition to the inner system.
